summary: Built and verified the CORP.EXAMPLE Samba AD environment. Both controllers are healthy and replicated, the engineering share is writable by infrasetuser, and DNS, authentication, and SMB access survived either controller being stopped independently.
actions_performed: Provisioned node1 and node2 as replicated Samba AD domain controllers.
Joined node3 as the member file server and node4 as the client.
Created engineering, infrasetuser, and the requested protected credential file.
Published /srv/corp/engineering with the requested content and write ACLs.
Bound identity services and routed domain DNS over enp8s0 on 10.100.80.0/24.
Stopped and restored each controller independently while testing live failover.

evidence.requirement: CORP.EXAMPLE replicated controllers on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: Node2 joined as a DC. Final checks on both controllers found 3,855 directory objects, zero database errors, `[ALL GOOD]` replication, and both LDAP SRV records.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated identity network for DNS, Kerberos, directory, and SMB
evidence.summary: Controller services listen on 10.100.80.10/11, node3 SMB listens on 10.100.80.12 with no egress-interface listener, and node4 routes DNS and SMB traffic through enp8s0.
The account was created and added to engineering; node2 independently showed the replicated user, membership, and account state.
Node3 and node4 reported successful joins, valid machine trust secrets, and working domain identity resolution.

evidence.requirement: Engineering share, welcome file, and member write access
evidence.summary: Final configuration shows the requested path, engineering-only write rules, ACLs, and exact `infraset-samba` content. A fresh Kerberos-authenticated engineering user created, listed, and removed a proof file.
`/root/corp-user.env` is root-owned mode 600, contains both requested variables, matches the AD credential, and successfully obtains Kerberos and CIFS tickets.

After a healthy baseline, node1 had no identity listeners. Node2 remained available, node3 moved its trust channel to node2, and node4 selected node2 DNS and completed fresh Kerberos plus SMB read/write operations. Node1 was restored with healthy replication and data.

Following an `[ALL GOOD]` baseline, node2 had no identity listeners. Node1 remained available, node3 moved its trust channel to node1, and node4 selected node1 DNS and completed fresh Kerberos plus SMB read/write operations. Node2 was restored and all naming contexts synchronized successfully in both directions.
